roadmap.goal: Story #6131 — the chart's bundled Postgres crosses a major version (17 → 18) by itself on a plain `helm upgrade`, `helm upgrade --reset-then-reuse-values` or a GitOps render, keeps the previous major's data untouched in `pgdata/` so `helm rollback` to 0.1.17 opens it again, and refuses every unsafe upgrade before writing anything (ADR-213 option B: two init containers from official images — `pg-old-binaries` on the upgrade-source image copies 17's bin/lib/share into an emptyDir, `pg-upgrade` on the main image decides and runs `pg_upgrade --copy` into `pgdata-<M>.partial/`, the rename to `pgdata-<M>/` is the commit, and the SHA-256 of the source `global/pg_control` in `pgdata-<M>/.lighthouse-upgrade` proves staleness). Commit a0766ed46 put the default back to `postgres:17` because main had 18 without the upgrade; step 01-01 moves it to `postgres:18-trixie` (upgrade source `postgres:17-trixie`) in the same commit that makes the upgrade work. Done when: every scenario in chart/tests/acceptance/upgrade-bundled-postgres.feature has lost its `@pending` tag and is green (kind scenarios through chart/tests/upgrade-path/run.sh in the `upgrade-path` job's `happy` and `refusals` legs, render scenarios in helm-unittest); `grep -n 'skip:' chart/tests/unit/postgres-upgrade_test.yaml` and `grep -n 'SCAFFOLD' chart/tests/upgrade-path/run.sh` return nothing; `helm lint` (default + enterprise values), `helm unittest -f 'tests/unit/*.yaml' ./chart`, shellcheck on every script and the helm-docs drift gate are green; `version-guard.sh` refuses a publish whose default Postgres major moved without the `pg-upgrade` init container; `upgrade-path` is in `publish.needs`. The `Release Notes` tag and line on ADO #6131, the chart version bump at `/release`, and the dogfood with a restored real backup are maintainer gates, deliberately NOT steps here.
roadmap.paradigm_note: EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM: Helm templates and a POSIX/bash init script have no property-test harness here; compensate with helm-unittest render properties across value combinations and kind scenarios with before/after volume hashes. The project is object-oriented, but this story adds no C# and no TypeScript, so there is no class design, no NUnit/Vitest test and no Stryker run (DEVOPS / Mutation Testing Strategy names the substitute: shellcheck, and every refusal scenario asserting the volume's sorted sha256sum listing is unchanged, which is the fault a mutant would plant). The crafter authors no new acceptance scenario: the Gherkin SSOT, the 15 helm-unittest cases (12 skipped, 3 running guards) and the 19 scaffold functions in run.sh were written by DISTILL. The crafter's RED is replacing a scaffold body (or removing a `skip:`) and watching it fail for the reason red-classification.md predicts — for the walking skeleton, the 18 pod crash-looping on `database files are incompatible with server` against the a0766ed46 chart with the image overridden to 18 — and its GREEN is the template/script change. One harness function has no scaffold and the crafter adds it: the AC-2.5 pin-back scenario (added to the feature by 8d7de4dda after run.sh was written). The crafter MAY add helm-unittest cases that widen a render property already specified (for example the image-major parser on a registry with a port), never a new behaviour. Each step's `scenario_name` is its primary scenario; every other scenario the step turns green is named, title verbatim, in its `unskips` list, and each of the 25 scenarios appears in exactly one step.

Checked against the code: (1) the feature file holds 25 scenarios (DISTILL's table lists 24; the AC-2.5 pin-back scenario was added by 8d7de4dda and has no run.sh function) — each is mapped to exactly one step; (2) chart/templates/postgres-statefulset.yaml has no initContainers and sets PGDATA=/var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata itself, so the wrapper must override PGDATA from the decision file; (3) version-guard.sh check 4 refuses an already-published version and main carries 0.1.17, which IS published — run the guard locally with a non-existent PUBLISHED_INDEX (`chart/scripts/version-guard.sh chart /nonexistent`) to reach the new check; (4) run.sh's HAPPY/REFUSALS arrays list all 19 scaffolds, so CI cannot run `run.sh CLUSTER happy` until the arrays list only implemented functions — 01-02 trims them and every later step appends; (5) render_test.yaml line 25 asserts `postgres:17` and moves with values.yaml in 01-01; (6) docs/Installation/kubernetes.md line 328 names `postgres:17` as today's default and moves in 01-01, the rest of the section is rewritten in 02-02; (7) DEVOPS placed the unclean-shutdown scenario (slice 01) in the `refusals` leg, so 01-02 creates both matrix legs, `refusals` holding only that scenario until phase 02 fills it; (8) Upstream finding 1 is decided (AC-2.5: start on the kept copy with one warning line) and is step 01-04; (9) every intermediate commit is data-safe: 01-01 refuses (one line, no write) every volume state its decision table does not handle yet, and later steps turn those states into their own rows, which is also what gives 01-02, 01-03, 01-04 and 02-03 a genuine RED.

user_decisions: D1 — automatic by default; no value switches it on.
D2 — the previous major's data is kept untouched so helm rollback works; about 2x the data on the PVC until the operator removes it.
D3 — refuse rather than half-upgrade: every refusal before any write, one log line naming reason and way out.
D4 — automatic source major = N-1; two or more majors behind is refused with a pointer to the manual path.
D5 — Postgres 18 becomes the chart default only in the same release as the upgrade (enforced from 01-06 by the version-guard check).
D6 — chart only; the docker-compose example keeps its manual path.
D7 — the same behaviour for helm upgrade and for a GitOps tool that renders the chart; no Helm hooks.
ADR-213 option B — two init containers from official images, pg_upgrade --copy, rename as commit, pg_control hash as staleness proof.
--reuse-values keeps the old image and does no upgrade; NOTES.txt prints one line saying the bundled Postgres is behind and naming --reset-then-reuse-values (AC-1.8).
AC-2.5 (decided 2026-10-02) — pinning the image back to the previous major on the new chart starts on the kept copy with one warning line.
out_of_scope: The docker-compose example and the binary/standalone server (D6).
External databases (postgresql.enabled=false) beyond proving they render as before.
Removing the old copy or growing the PVC automatically.
Downgrading data across majors; upgrades two or more majors apart (refused, D4).
arm64 runs (CI is amd64 only), settings made with ALTER SYSTEM (documented, not asserted), GitOps rollback by Git revert.
A digest pin on either Postgres image (not how the chart pins today).

Finalize-time and maintainer gates, not DELIVER steps: bumping Chart.yaml `version`/`appVersion` and cutting the release (/release); the `Release Notes` tag and line on ADO #6131; the dogfood on a kind cluster seeded from a real backup (DoD 3); reading K1 at 30 and 60 days; ADO state transitions.

phases.name: A plain helm upgrade carries a bundled Postgres 17 database to 18, and a rollback opens the old copy again
phases.description: Slice 01. Build the mechanism and prove the walking skeleton on kind first, with the default moved to postgres:18-trixie in the same commit; then wire CI so the proof repeats on every chart change, then extend the decision table one row at a time (restart, rollback and re-upgrade, pin-back), then the --reuse-values notes line, and last the release-safety rails (version-guard, validate checks, Renovate rule, Chart.yaml note). Every volume state the decision table does not handle yet is refused with one line and no write, so no intermediate commit can damage data even though main is unreleased.

steps.name: Walking skeleton: a plain helm upgrade from 0.1.17 with data comes back on Postgres 18 with every row
steps.description: Add the two init containers, the script ConfigMap and the start wrapper (DDD-1..8, 15, 16) and move the defaults to postgres:18-trixie / postgresql.upgrade.image postgres:17-trixie (DDD-11) in one commit. upgrade.sh handles exactly these rows of the decision table: fresh volume → `pgdata`; D = M with no `pgdata-*` → `pgdata`; D = M−1 with no `pgdata-M` (a leftover `.partial` is deleted first) → recovery if unclean (start 17 on a Unix socket only, fast stop), `initdb` into `pgdata-M.partial/` with the old cluster's checksums/encoding/locale/locale provider/bootstrap superuser, `pg_upgrade --copy`, copy `pg_hba.conf`/`pg_ident.conf`, write `.lighthouse-upgrade` (source major, system identifier, sha256 of `pgdata/global/pg_control` taken after pg_upgrade), fsync, rename → `pgdata-M`. EVERY other volume state goes through the one refusal path: one `lighthouse-postgres:` line naming what was found and that nothing was changed, the same line to the termination message, exit non-zero, before any write. Later steps turn specific states into their own rows. Implement the walking-skeleton, unclean-shutdown and fresh-install harness functions, and unskip the render tests this shape satisfies.

steps.implementation_notes: Order: write the walking-skeleton function and capture RED against today's chart, then templates and scripts, then unskip the render tests one group at a time. DESIGN measured the facts the scripts rely on (ADR-213 Context): 18's initdb turns checksums on (match the old cluster, read from `pg_controldata`); a bare initdb lacks the TCP scram rule (copy pg_hba.conf); the 0.1.17 pod usually ends unclean (a smart shutdown waits for pooled API connections). Read the bootstrap superuser (role OID 10) and template1's encoding/locale/provider from the old cluster after recovery and pass them to initdb. Pre-pull postgres:17-trixie, postgres:18-trixie and the 0.1.17 API image (26.9.24.6) on the host and `kind load docker-image` them. Use a fresh kind cluster per group locally (for example `kind create cluster --name lh-upgrade-happy`); never point anything at the dev instance on :5169. Keep the scripts plain and small enough to read; the decision table in feature-delta.md is the spec. Commit: `feat(chart): carry the bundled Postgres from 17 to 18 on helm upgrade, keeping the old copy (story 6131)`.
